Sort all the books into boxes by color: tap a box to lift the run of same-colored books on top, then tap another box to place them. The target box must be empty, or have the same color on top and room left. Each box holds up to 5 books, and five of one color seal the box automatically. Seal every book to clear the stage.
book-sort.view.21: Start with five fixed stages, then keep playing new numbered stages. More book colors appear at stages 6, 11 and 21. From stage 36 onward, you start with just one empty box. campaign.view.10: Hold to mute · Release to broadcast
campaign.view.11: The truck drives right and keeps speeding up. Release to broadcast for votes. Hold to mute near quiet zones at schools, hospitals and mansions.
campaign.view.12: Hold the screen, the mute button or
campaign.view.14: . The Upcoming display previews the next buildings. Disturbing a quiet zone or staying muted too long on a normal street counts as a mistake. Five mistakes end your campaign.
campaign.view.16: The truck drives right endlessly, speeding up from about 300 to 800 pixels per second (about 2.7×). Schools, hospitals and mansions are quiet zones marked by diagonal stripes on the road. Their share rises from about 30% to at most 60%, with at most two quiet buildings in a row.
campaign.view.17: Buildings appear early on the right, and Upcoming lists the next six. Release to broadcast; hold to mute. Normal buildings award votes in proportion to broadcast time, up to 200 votes. Broadcasting for less than 30% counts as a missed campaign stop and one mistake. In quiet zones, staying muted for at least 70% awards 100 votes; otherwise you disturb the zone, lose 400 votes and receive one mistake. Five mistakes end the round.
campaign.view.18: You start with 200 votes. Vote milestones award points immediately, kept after disqualification: 8,000 votes +3 points, 10,000 +7 (10 total), 12,000 +15, 15,000 +30, then +40 for every additional 3,000. These are fixed rewards, with no multiplier. Each milestone pays once per round; losing votes and regaining them does not pay again. Thresholds are deliberately high; a typical player is disqualified around 4,000–6,000 votes.
campaign.view.19: Switching games or hiding the tab pauses play and releases mute; hold again when you return. Refreshing abandons the round but keeps credited points. Points are shared and have no cash value.
campaign.view.21: Campaign Truck: drive right along the street; hold to mute at schools, hospitals and mansions

carp.view.12: ) to charge; release to jump. Too low hits rocks, too high catches hooks. The green zone in the power bar marks suitable power for the next obstacle. The carp looks more like a dragon at each milestone.

Too low hits rocks; Too high catches hooks. The green range on the left power bar shows suitable power for the next obstacle. Each waterfall cleared earns 1 score. Speed and difficulty gradually rise.
carp.view.19: BONUS: Cross 10, 20 and 35 waterfalls to earn 5 points at each milestone, credited immediately. Each milestone can be earned once per round, up to 15 points total. cat.view.05: Start the cat running across rooftops. Tap to jump. Milestone rewards are credited immediately and remain even if you fall later.
cat.view.07: Tap to jump; hold longer to jump higher. You can also use
cat.view.10: . Avoid gaps between rooftops and walls.
cat.view.19: The cat runs until it falls or hits a wall. Speed rises with distance and peaks around 700 m; rooftops get narrower and height differences grow. Tap or press Space to jump; hold longer to jump higher. Press just before landing to jump on touchdown. You can still jump within 0.14 seconds of leaving a rooftop edge. From 30 m, rooftops carry clutter, water tanks, laundry, low shop signs, tin roofs that collapse, and pigeons: hitting clutter, a sign, laundry or a pigeon trips the cat and slows it, and tripping twice within 4 seconds ends the run. Slide under signs, and jump off tin roofs right after landing.
cat.view.20: Milestones award points immediately, kept even after falling: 150 m +3, 300 m +7 (10 total), 500 m +15, 750 m +30, 1,000 m +60, then +40 per additional 250 m. These are fixed points, with no additional settlement on falling.
cat.view.21: These distances are deliberately demanding, requiring hundreds of accurate jumps. A typical player struggles to pass 300 m; only highly skilled players see 1,000 m. Results depend on jump timing and how long you hold.
cat.view.22: Switching games or hiding the tab pauses play; return to continue. Refreshing abandons the round but keeps credited rewards. Your best record is saved in this browser. Points are shared and have no cash value.
cat.view.23: Rooftop Cat: tap to jump, hold longer to jump higher, and avoid gaps between rooftops
cat.view.26: Keys: Space, W or ↑ to jump; S or ↓ to slide. On a phone, swipe down to slide.
clock-out.view.06: place tools in the drawer, then start work. Clear Wave 5 for +3 pts, and clearing the day gives +7 more.
clock-out.view.07: Placement phase: tap a card, then a drawer cell to place it. Touching tools of the same type and level merge and upgrade. R rotates, Delete recycles, Enter starts work. Battle phase: tap the field to throw sticky notes and help out.
clock-out.view.09: The day has 8 waves (09:00 to 16:00). Before each wave, place Rubber Bands, Coffee Mugs, Staplers, Highlighters, Headphones, Stamps and Shredders in the 6×6 drawer, then start work. Emails, papers, meetings, reports and urgent tasks walk along the desk toward your seat; Each one that gets through costs sanity. The round ends when sanity hits zero or the boss reaches your desk. Sanity recovers 2 points after each wave.
clock-out.view.10: Each tool counters a different enemy. Coffee Mugs and Highlighters also boost the attack tools next to them. Tools of the same type and level can merge, up to Lv.3. A meeting locks the nearest attack tool; place Headphones beside it to avoid the lock.
clock-out.view.11: BONUS is a fixed reward: surviving Wave 5 credits 3 pts immediately, and beating the boss in Wave 8 credits 7 more. Each is paid once per round, for 10 points in total. Rewards are credited on the spot and never taken back if you lose later. If you leave or reload, credited points stay. Score is for display only and does not convert to points. This is a skill and placement-strategy game: results depend on how you place tools and play.
clock-out.view.12: Switching games or backgrounding the tab pauses the round and resumes when you return. Your best score is saved in this browser; points are shared with the other games and have no cash value.
clock-out.view.13: Clock Out: place office supplies in the drawer grid as defenses, tap the field to throw sticky notes, and survive until 17:00
crash.view.07: Dive deeper for a higher multiplier; surface before the hull collapses.
crash.view.14: Each round has a six-second betting window. The diving multiplier starts at 1.00× and rises by 1× per 1,000 m. Surface before the crash to collect bet × current multiplier. Otherwise you lose the bet.
crash.view.15: The crash point is determined before diving:
crash.view.17: , where r is uniform from 0 to 1. A round therefore has a 3% chance to crash immediately at 1.00×. Expected return is about 97% regardless of your chosen surface multiplier.
crash.view.18: This is a browser-only demo. Points have no cash value and your balance is stored only in this browser.
crossing.view.01: Help the turtle cross twelve currents from the left
crossing.view.14: Each crossing raises the multiplier, but any crossing may hide a current. Decide when to collect.
crossing.view.16: The turtle starts at the left. Each Advance crosses one current. A safe crossing increases the multiplier; a current loses the bet. After each crossing you can collect bet × current multiplier. Twelve crossings collect automatically.
crossing.view.17: You do not choose cells, only whether to advance. Difficulty sets each crossing's success chance: Easy 92%, Medium 85%, Hard 75%, Extreme 60%. After all twelve crossings, the multipliers are 2.63×, 6.82×, 30.62× and 445.62× respectively.
crossing.view.18: The multiplier is 0.97 divided by the crossing chance raised to the number of crossings, giving an expected return of about 97% regardless of difficulty or when you collect. The browser determines the current location when you start; a dashed line marks it afterward. Points are shared with other games and have no cash value.
dice.view.13: Adjust the threshold: lower win chance means a higher multiplier.
dice.view.15: Each sonar reading is uniformly drawn from 0.00 to 99.99: 10,000 equally likely results. Choose a threshold, then predict below it or at/above it (equality counts as above). The bright range is your winning range.
dice.view.16: Below T wins with T% probability; T or above wins with (100 − T)%. The multiplier is
dice.view.18: , so expected return is about 97% for every threshold. Win chance ranges from 2% to 95%, corresponding to 48.50× to 1.02×.
dice.view.19: Browser randomness determines the reading when you click. Points are shared with other games and have no cash value.
dive.view.06: Select Start diving or Take a deep breath inside the game. Only your record is saved; No extra achievement rewards are paid.
dive.view.07: Choose routes downward. Oxygen must exceed the red line to surface and record your score; drowning gives zero. If you discard pearls to surface, the final results show the actual score.
dive.view.09: Choose a route each floor to dive, spending oxygen and possibly finding pearls, oxygen or relics. The red line shows oxygen needed to surface; More pearls raise it. You need oxygen above the line to surface. Discard some pearls to lighten the load if necessary.
dive.view.10: Score = pearls + floors × 2. Surfacing or reaching floor 40 ends the dive and records your best score. Running out of oxygen gives zero score; the Lifeline relic saves half your pearls the first time. Score does not convert to wallet points. There are no point multipliers or collection payouts.
dive.view.11: This game is turn-based. Leaving does not end the round; return to continue. Refreshing abandons it with earned rewards retained. Best score is saved in this browser. Shared points have no cash value.
dream.view.04: The needle spins when you start. Stop it in the teal zone to clear the stage.
dream.view.06: Select Stop, tap the dial or press
dream.view.08: After clearing a stage, select Next stage to continue.
dream.view.10: Continuing is unlimited and stages are endless. Stop the needle in the teal zone to advance. A miss ends the round. No extra achievement rewards are paid, and stage scores do not become wallet points.
dream.view.11: The target zone narrows to at least 24° and the needle speeds up to 2.4 radians per second. From stage 11 it can reverse once per stage; from stage 21, twice. Before reversing, the center light and message warn for at least 0.5 seconds. Reversals are delayed near the target and spaced at least 1.5 seconds apart, without changing speed. Narrowing and acceleration ease briefly when reversals are introduced.
dream.view.12: Switching games, hiding the tab or losing focus pauses play; return to continue. Time waiting between stages is not counted as active play. Refreshing abandons the round. Points are shared and have no cash value.
dream.view.13: Dream Repair: stop the needle in the teal target zone
eat-smaller.view.06: On a computer your number swims toward the mouse, or use the arrow keys or WASD; on a phone press and drag anywhere like a joystick. Your first move starts the stage. R restarts, P or Esc opens stage select, M toggles sound.
eat-smaller.view.08: You are a number. Touch a smaller green number to eat it and add its value to yours; touch a bigger red number and you get eaten. Operators (−3, +1, ÷2) take effect on contact and can bring you back down when you overshoot. You must hit the target exactly to clear the stage, and the bigger you get, the slower you swim. There are 12 stages; clearing one unlocks the next.
eat-smaller.view.09: Within a round you can pick and replay stages freely, and retrying after a loss costs nothing extra. BONUS is a fixed reward: The first time you clear each stage in the round adds 2 pts right away; Clearing the same stage again in that round pays nothing, up to Points already added are never taken back, and nothing extra is paid at the end. Press “End round” to finish; Earning BONUS again needs a new round. Clear times are records only and never convert to points; This is a skill and arithmetic game with no betting or multiplier payouts.
eat-smaller.view.10: Switching games or moving the tab to the background pauses the game; Press “Resume” when you’re back. Reloading abandons the round: BONUS points already added are kept. Stage progress and best times are saved in this browser; Points are shared with the other games and have no cash value.
elevator.view.16: Each tap passes one person. Being seen by any passenger ahead while moving ends the round; staying still is safe.
elevator.view.17: Tap Pass one person, the game screen or press
elevator.view.19: . A warning alone does not catch you, but there is no guaranteed safe interval.
elevator.view.21: Each round play from the shared wallet. Passengers independently switch between looking away, warning and watching. A warning may clear or become a glance at any moment. Moving while anyone ahead is watching gets you caught. Staying still is safe.
elevator.view.22: Each tap passes one person in about 0.4–0.7 seconds; being seen during that movement also ends the round. Reaching the front immediately starts a new queue. The first has 10 people, with 2 added per queue up to 30. Rest intervals shrink and warnings more often turn into glances. Play until caught.
elevator.view.23: Passing enough people earns immediate milestone rewards: 40 people +3 points, 55 +7 (10 total), 70 +15, 90 +30, then +40 for every additional 20. Rewards remain after you are caught. These are fixed points, with no multiplier. Thresholds are deliberately high; a typical player passes about 25 people.
elevator.view.24: Switching games or hiding the tab pauses play. Refreshing abandons the round but keeps credited points. Points are shared and have no cash value.
elevator.view.26: Queue Cutter: pass people while they look away in ever-longer lines; warnings may turn into glances
fishing.view.09: Cast first, then watch the fish
fishing.view.13: Hold to reel · Release to ease tension
fishing.view.14: Cast first, then hold to reel. Release during struggles to ease tension and avoid snapping the line.
fishing.view.15: Hold the screen, the reel button or
fishing.view.17: . Release too long and the fish swims away; too little tension can lose the hook.
fishing.view.19: Holding to reel brings the fish closer but raises tension; Releasing eases tension but lets it swim away. Reel during steady swimming; Prepare to release when splashes grow. Reeling during violent struggles quickly raises tension; Tired fish are easiest to reel in.
fishing.view.20: Each landed fish is immediately followed by another. The round ends on a snapped line or lost hook. Larger fish start farther away, struggle longer and increase tension faster when pulled; difficulty stops increasing around fish 20. Tension 100 snaps the line. Tension at or below 8 for 1.2 seconds loses the hook. Stalling and releasing do not help.
fishing.view.21: Fish milestones award points immediately, kept even after a snapped line: 10 fish +3 points, 12 +7 (10 total), 14 +15, 17 +30, then +40 for every additional 3 fish. These are fixed points, with no multiplier. Thresholds are deliberately high; a typical player catches about 8 fish.
fishing.view.22: Switching games or hiding the tab pauses play and releases the reel; Hold again when you return. Losing focus also releases the reel. Refreshing abandons the round but keeps credited points. Points are shared; The reset remains for testing.
fishing.view.24: Fishing: hold to reel, release to ease tension and land the fish
frog.view.06: The frog is hungry! Start, then press when the arrow aligns with the lowest bug.
frog.view.10: or tap to stick out your tongue. Align with the center of the lowest bug. Yellow flashes warn of anger; do not eat red spiky bugs. Wait for them to turn pink. Eating during the yellow warning gives extra score.
frog.view.12: Bugs form a tower; A yellow arrow moves between the lowest two. Press Space or tap when it aligns with the lowest bug's center to eat it. Better alignment gives more score. A miss costs no hearts, but briefly pauses play, resets your combo and costs a little fullness.
frog.view.13: Pink bugs with eyebrows get angry: they flash yellow for half a second, then turn red and spiky. Eating a red bug stings and costs one heart. Wait until it turns pink again. Eating during the yellow warning earns extra score.
frog.view.14: Fullness constantly falls; eat bugs to refill it. No hearts or zero fullness ends the round. Every 10 bugs raises your level, speeds up the arrow, adds angry bugs, restores some fullness and immediately awards 1 point, kept when the round ends. Score and combos do not convert to points. Results depend on timing.
frog.view.15: Switching games or hiding the tab pauses play; return to continue. Refreshing abandons the round. credited points remain. Your best record is saved in this browser. Points are shared and have no cash value.
frog.view.16: Frog Snack: press Space or tap when aligned with the lowest bug; avoid red spiky bugs
frontier.view.01: Ranked expeditions keep verified progress. You can return to your local save at any time.
frontier.view.08: Establish an outpost, defeat the guards, restore the beacon.
frontier.view.09: Coins full! Pick an upgrade card
frontier.view.11: Five regions. Fifty trials. Build a foothold and cross dangerous lands.
frontier.view.24: Buy equipment near camp and sell stored materials near the market. Gold is used only in this game.
frontier.view.26: From stage 11, build barracks and spend stored wood and stone to train warriors who defend HQ automatically. You lose when HQ health reaches zero.
frontier.view.34: Replay an unlocked stage. Confirming replaces your current island progress.
frontier.view.38: Approach resources to gather and foundations to build. Cottages recruit gatherers and haulers. Approach ground resources or a carrying worker to collect supplies; full bags leave supplies intact. The quarry adds a stone worker, the mill improves efficiency, and towers defend the village.
frontier.view.39: After defeating monsters, walk up to pick up the coins; when the meter fills, three upgrade cards appear and you pick one to strengthen your hero, warriors or towers. Standing next to the barracks trains warriors automatically. Repair damaged buildings by standing near them and spending stored wood. Raids are announced with a countdown.
frontier.view.40: Move to gather, build and attack automatically. Use WASD / arrow keys, drag the joystick, or tap the ground to walk there.
frontier.view.42: Expeditions, all 50 stages, retries and saved games are, with no extra achievement payout. Equipment, gold and highest stage persist; Local materials and buildings reset on each island. Progress saves every five seconds and on pause. Switching games or hiding the page pauses play; Resume manually. Saves stay in this browser.
frontier.view.43: Five regions have ten stages each, mixing construction, rescue, combat, defense and elite missions, with a boss every ten stages. Build a tower for defense missions. Complete village and mission requirements to build the beacon, then choose when to depart. Later enemies have shorter warnings and mixed formations. Region three adds amber ground warnings. Frost slows movement without a forge. Night increases enemy speed up to a cap, without a hidden timeout.
frontier.view.45: The board is an art direction reference. The playable scene is drawn with Canvas.
frontier.view.47: Frontier Islands: move to gather, approach to build, dodge attacks
frontier.view.50: Frontier Islands art reference: explorer, trees, rocks and chopping feedback
hilo.view.01: Will the next card be higher or lower?
hilo.view.11: Start to reveal the first card. Each correct guess increases the multiplier; collect at any time.
hilo.view.13: Ranks are A, 2 … 10, J, Q, K, with A lowest. Start to reveal a card, then guess whether the next is higher/equal (Rise) or lower/equal (Fall). Correct guesses compound the multiplier. Continue or collect bet × current multiplier; a wrong guess loses the bet.
hilo.view.14: With A, Rise means strictly higher and Fall means equal. With K the reverse applies. You can change cards three times per round without changing the multiplier.
hilo.view.15: Each card is drawn independently and uniformly from 13 ranks, as with unlimited decks. Multipliers compound as 1 ÷ correct-guess probability, then multiply by 0.97, giving an expected return of about 97%. Buttons show the probability and resulting multiplier.
keno.view.11: Five digs per attempt, one cell at a time. How many minerals can you find?
keno.view.13: Three attempts per day, with five digs each. Each shuffled 36-cell mine has 18 rocks, 10 copper, 6 gold and 2 diamonds. Rocks give 0 points, copper 2, gold 3 and diamonds 5, credited immediately. You can earn up to 30 points daily. Near the cap, only the remaining allowance is credited; Reaching the cap completes today's supply.
keno.view.14: Resets at midnight Taiwan time. An attempt is used when you start; refreshing lets you finish its remaining digs without duplicating rewards. Records are stored only in this browser, with no cross-device sync. There are no paid extra digs. Score and best score are separate from wallet points.
last-hair.view.05: Sato has only 3 hairs left and an interview today! Head out, tilt into the wind, press your hair down, and walk 500 m.
last-hair.view.06: Mobile: slide the neck on the left half of the screen to move the slider into the green ring; hold "HOLD" on the right half. Desktop:
last-hair.view.08: , or move the mouse left and right) to tilt your head; hold
last-hair.view.10: or mouse to press the hair. Tilting too long cramps your neck; pressing too long makes your hand sweat and passers-by stare.
last-hair.view.12: Sato has only 3 hairs left and must walk 500 m through a gale to his interview. Tilting your neck toward the wind reduces exposure; Pressing your head blocks most of the wind and slowly restores the gel. Each of the three hairs has gel (yellow bar) and a root (red bar). The gel drains first, then the root; When one is gone it flies away with a "pop", and when all three are gone the interview is cancelled. The fewer hairs you have left, the slower you walk.
last-hair.view.13: Tilting past 85% for 3 seconds in a row cramps your neck and freezes it for 2 seconds. Pressing builds up hand sweat, and a full sweat meter means you can no longer press. Passers-by stare while you press; a full stare meter means social death, which slows your steps and forces your hand down for 1.5 seconds. Each of the four sections has its own events: greetings on the shopping street (let go for 1.2 seconds to count as a wave) and flyers (hand occupied for 2 seconds), dripping water under the overpass (blocked by pressing) and pigeon turbulence, and the downdraft and the interviewer turning around on the plaza (pressing then draws stares). Every event gives a warning first.
last-hair.view.14: Reaching 100, 250, 400 and 500 m credits 1, 2, 3 and 4 points immediately. Each milestone pays once per run, 10 points in total. Losing all your hair does not take back points already credited. The ending and hair count only change your title and give no points. Distance is only a record and is not exchanged for points. This is a skill game with no multipliers.
last-hair.view.15: Switching games or background tabs pauses the run; tap the screen to resume. Refreshing abandons the run: points already credited are kept. Best distance, death spots and control settings are stored in your browser. Points are shared with other games and have no cash value.
last-hair.view.17: Dignity Defense: slide the neck with your left hand to tilt into the wind and press the hair with your right; walk 500 m to the interview with at least one hair left

limbo.view.11: Higher targets are harder to reach; a win pays your target multiplier.

market-desk.view.05: A rented desk, a cup of coffee, and twenty days to prove himself.
market-desk.view.09: One more miss ends the run
market-desk.view.12: Your first market report after quitting
market-desk.view.13: You quit with your year-end bonus and give yourself 20 trading days to put together a market report. From breakfast-shop tips to quantum dumplings, what belongs in print?
market-desk.view.23: Publish verified details, hold stories that lack evidence, and warn readers about impersonation or requests for credentials.
market-desk.view.24: A correct call earns 5 score and restores 4 focus, up to 100 focus. A wrong call costs 18 focus. The run ends at zero focus or after 20 days.
merge.view.06: Slide matching pearls together to merge larger pearls.
merge.view.12: Start round play. Each swipe slides all pearls in one direction. Matching pearls merge into double their value and add that value to your score. Each move spawns a 2 (90%) or a 4 (10%).
merge.view.13: The round ends when the board is full and no neighboring pearls match.
merge.view.14: Your best score is saved only in this browser.
merge.view.17: Keep playing after reaching 2048. The guest leaderboard ranks your largest pearl in a completed round.
mermaid.view.01: Deal, then line cards up into a full run to collect a pearl.
mermaid.view.05: Build same-suit runs from K down to A and collect 8 pearls.
mermaid.view.18: BONUS +1 point for every pearl you collect.
mermaid.view.19: Drag a card, or tap a card and then tap the target column to move it. Only same-suit, high-to-low runs move together. Tap the deck at the top left to deal; the hint shows you a good move.
mermaid.view.21: The table has 10 columns and 104 cards with mermaid card backs. Place a card on a card one rank higher (any suit); Same-suit runs in descending order can move together. A full 13-card K to A run in one suit is collected automatically as a pearl. Collect 8 pearls to clear the round. Tap the deck to deal one card to every column; Every column must have a card before you deal.
mermaid.view.22: There are three difficulties: Shallows has 1 suit, Coral Reef 2 and Deep Sea 4. Pick before starting; It cannot change once the round starts. Undo and hints are unlimited and cost no points, but every move (undo included) lowers your score by 1, and each pearl adds 100. Score is for display only and is not exchanged for points.
mermaid.view.23: Each pearl you collect pays a BONUS of +1 point on the spot; clearing Coral Reef or Deep Sea adds +2 points once. So the most you can be credited is 8 points on Shallows and 10 points on Coral Reef or Deep Sea, with no betting or multipliers. Undoing and collecting the same pearl again does not pay twice. This is a skill and reasoning solitaire.
mermaid.view.24: Giving up keeps points already credited. Refreshing the page abandons the round. Best scores are saved per difficulty in your browser; points are shared with the other games and have no cash value.
mermaid.view.28: Mermaid Spider table: stack cards from high to low, and a full K to A in one suit becomes a pearl
mines.view.14: Turn on Flag to tap cells to place or remove flags. Turn it off to reveal cells.
mines.view.15: Tap to reveal. Touch and hold to flag or unflag; right-click on desktop. Keyboard: press F on a cell.
mines.view.16: When adjacent flags match a number, tap it to reveal its neighbors. Incorrect flags can still hit a mine.
mines.view.17: Mines are placed at random, so the first move can hit a mine. Numbers count neighboring mines and empty areas open automatically. Reveal every safe cell to win.
mines.view.18: Clear a 5×5 board with 3 mines to rank. Scroll sideways on larger boards. Reloading ends the round.
mirror-twins.view.06: The arrow keys or WASD move both astronauts at once; on a phone, swipe on the screen or use the arrow pad. Z undoes, R restarts, Esc returns to stage select.
mirror-twins.view.08: You control two astronauts at once: blue moves the way you press, orange moves the same up and down but with left and right reversed. Whoever bumps into an asteroid stays put while the other keeps moving, which is how you pull them apart. Both must stand in their own colour’s teleporter at the same time to clear the stage; stepping on a laser mine undoes the move automatically. There are 10 stages; clearing one unlocks the next, with 1–3 stars based on your moves.
mirror-twins.view.09: Within a round you can pick and replay stages freely, and retrying after a loss costs nothing extra. BONUS is a fixed reward: The first time you clear each stage in the round adds 2 pts right away; Clearing the same stage again in that round pays nothing, up to Points already added are never taken back, and nothing extra is paid at the end. Press “End round” to finish; Earning BONUS again needs a new round. Stars, moves and clear times are records only and never convert to points; This is a skill and logic game with no betting or multiplier payouts.
mirror-twins.view.10: This game is turn-based, so leaving the screen doesn’t affect the board; Pick up where you left off. Reloading abandons the round: BONUS points already added are kept. Stage progress and best stars are saved in this browser; Points are shared with the other games and have no cash value.
mosquito.view.05: The mosquito is ready! Start, release Space to rise, hold to dive, and land on skin and hold to feed.
mosquito.view.08: or hold the screen to dive; release to drift up. Land on the cheek, arm or foot and keep holding to feed; release to take off. The more you drink, the heavier you get. When a red ripple appears on the skin, let go at once; when the blanket bulges, fly up; when alertness is full, the light comes on.
mosquito.view.10: You are a mosquito in the dead of night: Drink your fill from the sleeper, then escape through the hole in the top-left window. Release Space to drift up and hold to dive. Land on the cheek, arm or foot and keep holding to start feeding; Release to take off. Land too fast and the mosquito snaps its mouthpart and is stunned for 1 second.
mosquito.view.11: The more you drink, the heavier the mosquito gets: it rises slower and dives faster. Alertness climbs as you fly and feed: the face is fastest and loudest, the foot slowest and quietest, and flying near his ears or up high is louder too. Once feeding reaches 90%, alertness rises at half speed.
mosquito.view.12: The sleeper has three ways to swat you. When a red ripple appears on the skin while you feed, a giant hand comes down 1.2 seconds later, so let go and fly away at once. A bulging blanket means he is about to roll over, and the whole lower part of the screen will be crushed, so fly up first. When alertness is full the light comes on: you have 4.5 seconds to fly into the hole in the top-left window to survive, but escaping without a full belly does not clear the round.
mosquito.view.13: Fixed BONUS: when feeding reaches 25%, 50% and 75%, 1, 2 and 3 points are credited immediately; fill to 100% and fly out of the window to be credited 4 more points, up to 10 points per run. Each threshold pays once per round, points already credited are not taken back if you are swatted, and nothing more is settled at the end. Feeding percentage and best record are only records and are not exchanged for points. This is a skill game; the result depends on your timing.
mosquito.view.14: Switching games or hiding the tab pauses play; return to continue. Refreshing abandons the round. credited points remain. Your best record is saved in this browser. Points are shared and have no cash value.
mosquito.view.16: Midnight Mosquito: release Space to rise, hold to dive, land on skin and hold to feed, then fly out through the hole in the top-left window
mosquito.view.19: The mosquito flies left and right by itself. You only control height: hold to dive, release to rise.
mosquito.view.20: Yellow arrows mark skin you can feed on: face, arm and foot. Land gently or you will be stunned. Keep holding to feed; release to take off.
mosquito.view.21: Red ripples on the skin mean a slap is coming. Release and fly away at once.
mosquito.view.22: A red dashed line means he is about to roll over. Fly above the line.
mosquito.view.23: At full alert the light comes on. Escape through the top-left hole within 4.5 seconds: release to rise, then tap near the green dashed lines to stay between them.
mosquito.view.24: You clear the round only if you fill up to 100% and then fly out through the hole.
mrt.view.06: Select Board or Board train inside the game. Each seat gained advances one tier. Only your record is saved; No extra achievement rewards are paid.
mrt.view.07: Watch gestures and belongings, then tap a seat to stand there. Zero stamina or tier 8 ends the ride.
mrt.view.09: Before the train arrives, watch passengers' gestures and belongings. Tap to stand in front of someone you think will get off. A correct guess gains a seat and tier; A miss costs stamina for standing a whole stop. Zero stamina ends the round.
mrt.view.10: Rest while seated, then stand to compete for the next tier. Higher tiers bring faster arrivals, less reliable clues and more rivals. Tier 8 or the last train's final stop ends the ride and saves your best tier. Tiers are records, not wallet points; there are no point multipliers or collection payouts.
mrt.view.11: Switching games or hiding the tab pauses an arriving train. Select Continue when you return. Refreshing abandons the round with earned rewards retained. Best tier is saved in this browser. Shared points have no cash value.

nap.view.10: or the large bottom-left button to sleep. Press
nap.view.11: or the bottom-right button to throw trash. Longer naps fill sleepiness faster but take longer to wake from. Release immediately at “!”. Stun the boss with trash to nap safely.
nap.view.13: Hold Sleep at your desk to fill the sleepiness bar and clear each of 10 stages while the boss patrols. A red “!” warns before he looks. If he sees you sleeping, still waking up or throwing trash, you lose one performance mark and some sleepiness. Lose all marks and you are fired; The round ends.

Each hit makes his next glance earlier, so throwing carelessly makes him turn sooner. From stage 3, some warnings are feints. From stage 5, he may look back a second time.
nap.view.15: Each cleared stage immediately awards 1 point, kept when the round ends. Ten stages give 10 points total. Score does not convert to points. Results depend on when you release the button.

nap.view.18: Nap Master: hold Sleep, release at the boss's warning, and throw trash to stun him at zero health

ocean-link.view.20: Easy mode has larger tiles and classic matching in every stage, ideal for beginners.
ocean-link.view.21: Play 10 stages per expedition. Clear stages 3, 6, and 10 to earn 5 points each, once per stage and up to 15 points per expedition.

office-shoot.view.08: , or move the mouse left and right; on phones, press and drag on the screen. The shift ends when work in the right lane reaches the clock-out line; break the shields on supply crates in the left lane for new gear or boosts.

office-shoot.view.11: The screen has two lanes: On the right, work keeps pouring in (reports, urgent tasks, meetings…), and if any of it crosses the red clock-out line you’re working overtime tonight and the shift ends. The left lane is the supply station: Falling supply crates carry shields, and breaking them upgrades your gear (Ballpoint Pen, Stapler, Shredder, Laser Pointer, Coffee Rocket, Printer, Seen-Zone Cannon) or gives boosts such as fire rate, damage or an extra hand. You fire automatically; Just move left and right and choose between the lanes.
office-shoot.view.12: Each day starts at 9 AM, and at 5 PM that day’s boss shows up with its own trick: splitting, periodic invincibility, dumping to-dos, a single weak spot, absorbing bullets while changing requirements, healing when you stop firing, real and fake twins, throwing paperwork, warping in with backup, and message missiles. Days 1–10 have fixed bosses; after that, bosses mix 2–3 random tricks. Beating the boss means you clocked out on time and move on to the next day, and the enemies keep getting tougher.
office-shoot.view.13: BONUS is a fixed reward: on days 1–5, each time you beat that day’s boss (clock out on time) 2 pts are credited right away, once per day per shift, up to 10 pts per shift. From day 6 you can keep chasing your best score, but no more points are given. Credited points are never taken back if you end up working overtime later, and nothing extra is paid when the shift ends. Score, gear and boosts are in-game values only and never convert to points. This is a skill game with no betting or payout multipliers.
office-shoot.view.14: Switching games, moving the tab to the background or leaving the window pauses the shift; tap the screen or press Space to resume. Refreshing abandons the shift: the entry is not refunded and credited BONUS points are kept. Your best score is saved in this browser; points are shared with the other games and have no cash value.
office-shoot.view.15: No Overtime!: move left and right while firing automatically, stop the work flooding the right lane, break left-lane supplies for new gear, and beat the 5 PM boss each day to clock out on time
on-pitch.view.10: Sing, hum or whistle the note in the wall gap. Get your pitch into range and hold it briefly to pass; a wrong or missed note costs a heart, and you fail when all three are gone. Headphones help: the reference tone from your speakers can be picked up by the microphone (detection pauses while a tone plays). On a computer you can also practice with the keys C D E F G A B (or 1–7); pause with ❚❚ on screen or Esc.
on-pitch.view.12: You are a little robot gliding forward while walls with a gap keep arriving. The height of the gap matches one of seven notes, C D E F G A B (octave 4). Sing that note into the microphone, keep your pitch within the tolerance and hold it for 0.2–0.25 seconds to slip through. If you have not hit the note by the time the wall passes, you lose one of your 3 hearts. A pass is graded Perfect, Good or OK by how close you were, and passes in a row build your combo score.
on-pitch.view.13: There are 5 worlds of 4 levels each, plus an endless mode. World 1 gives every cue (gap height, note name, color and a reference tone); World 2 has you sing public-domain tunes such as Twinkle Twinkle; World 3 hides the gap height; World 4 leaves only a color flash; World 5 removes cues step by step so you rely on memory and absolute pitch. Later worlds allow less error (±45 down to ±30 cents). By default “Any octave” only checks the note name, so a higher or lower octave counts; you can switch to strict octave 4.
on-pitch.view.14: This game has no BONUS. Score and stars are only your results and never turn into points; there is no betting or multiplier payout. The first time you finish a round of each game each day (at least 10 seconds), you receive the platform’s fixed completion reward.
on-pitch.view.15: The microphone is only analyzed live for pitch during play; nothing is recorded or uploaded. Switching tabs, leaving this page or pausing turns the microphone off immediately. Stars and settings are saved in this browser.
on-pitch.view.16: Stay On Pitch: sing the note in the wall gap (C D E F G A B) into the microphone to pass through; or practice with the on-screen keys
one-line-defense.view.05: Press and drag on the left to draw a line; enemies that touch it are wiped out. Drawing a new line erases the old one, and shorter lines last longer. Mouse and finger both work.
one-line-defense.view.07: Enemies swarm the core in the middle from every direction, and you can only have one line at a time. Drag to draw a line; enemies that touch it are wiped out. The longer the line, the faster it fades: a short line lasts several seconds, a big loop less than 1 second. The more enemies one line wipes out in a row, the bigger the combo score (game score only). Big enemies break your line, and purple ones split when hit. The game ends when the core is hit five times. Your first game starts with a tutorial, during which the core can’t be hurt and the clock doesn’t run.
one-line-defense.view.08: BONUS is a fixed reward: After the tutorial, every 30 seconds survived adds 2 pts right away, once each at 30 / 60 / 90 / 120 / 150 seconds, up to 10 pts per game. Points already added are not taken back when the core later falls, and nothing extra is paid at the end. Score, combos and survival time are records only and never convert to points; This is a skill game with no betting or multiplier payouts.
one-line-defense.view.09: Switching games or moving the tab to the background pauses the game; Press “Resume” when you’re back. Reloading abandons the game: BONUS points already added are kept. Your best score is saved in this browser; Points are shared with the other games and have no cash value.
outpost.view.35: Stage 1 counts toward the guest leaderboard.
outpost.view.50: After starting, select a device and tap an empty pad.
outpost.view.55: Hold the station for 3 minutes. Enemies move from right to left. Each breach costs 1 hull. Stage 1 starts with 95 energy. Gain 5 energy every 4 seconds.
outpost.view.56: Bubble Cannons hit nearby targets too. Sonar Towers mark enemies so they take extra damage. Pulse Coils work well against armor.
outpost.view.57: Choose a direction before building a gate. When enemies approach, tap the built gate to divert the group into the neighboring lane. Gates recharge in 8 seconds.
outpost.view.58: Defeating a diverted enemy adds 15 to your score. Surviving 3 minutes adds 300, plus 100 per remaining hull.
outpost.view.59: From stage 2, from wave 2, tap a deployed Bubble Cannon or Pulse Coil to upgrade it once for 25 energy. Cannons gain splash range and coils fire faster.
outpost.view.60: All 30 stages unlock one by one. Later stages bring bigger, tougher swarms, and in the late stages even ordinary enemies swim faster, while energy income rises only slightly.
outpost.view.61: Armored crabs have 85 HP. Put a Sonar Tower and a Pulse Coil in the same lane so the coil can hit marked crabs.
pancake.view.01: Start, replay and refill noodles. Active play earns platform points.
pancake.view.03: Midnight noodle pancakes: shake to move the pancake and flick up when the rim is golden. Touch controls work without motion sensors.
peek.view.20: Something is chasing you. You run automatically once you start; swipe left or right to hide in a spot by the road.
peek.view.21: Keyboard: ← → hide in a roadside tree or coffin; F picks things up and leaves your hiding spot; 1–4 or T use the items at the top right.
peek.view.22: Phone: swipe left or right to hide; tap to pick things up and leave your hiding spot; tap an item slot at the top right to use it.
peek.view.23: When a ghost shows up, items appear on both sides: tap the right one. Do not stay hidden too long, or Dread catches up from behind. Headphones recommended.
peek.view.26: Direction captions (text shows where sounds come from)
peek.view.30: There are 100 levels in five worlds (forest, graveyard, swamp, snowfield, volcano), 20 levels per world. Every level has its own type and weather (day, dusk, night, rain, fog, snow, ash, heat and so on; never the same twice in a row). New ghosts appear on levels 4, 8, 12 and 16, and level 10 is the boss. Some levels have a chest, a traveler or the little critter Nib. You have 3 lives (max 5); if you die you retry the same level, and when you run out you start over from level 1 with no checkpoint. Beating a boss adds a life, and resting at a campfire can restore one life (at most once per ten levels). After two deaths on the same level, Flick gives you 0.3 s more warning and one attack fewer (the screen tells you). Level 1 and boss levels use a fixed seed, other levels are random; enter a seed code to replay the same round, or pick the daily challenge (same level and seed for everyone that day; no life lost, no save, no points, just a score to compare). You can only choose up to the level you actually reached this run; once your lives run out you the whole run restarts and you cannot jump back. Every level sends all its attacks before the door opens. Level 0 is a free run with no lives; in the codex you can listen to the clues and practice a ghost, with no lives lost and no points paid.
peek.view.31: You run through the forest with the box toward the exit. There is no progress bar: when you can see the exit, you are almost there. Trees and coffins slide into view from the left or right just before a ghost appears; swipe sideways to hide in one. Hiding spots are not always there. Some ghosts double back several times, and a pass only ends when the crickets return. The view is first-person and the background is the world of the current level.
peek.view.32: Every ghost has its own clue and answer. Leafling (level 4): the leaves pile up at your feet and a red eye opens; hide on the other side and hold on for 3 seconds. Knocker (level 8): the birds fly off, then knocking comes from one side; hide on the side opposite the knocking; later levels come back for two passes. Hush (level 12): the crickets stop and a prop appears on each side; it fears the lantern, so tap the lantern's side. Tapping the wrong one kills you. Gale (level 16): the wind reverses and leaves turn against it, then dragging approaches from one side; hide on the side the wind comes from. Reacher (level 22): the soil bulges and mud bubbles; hide on the other side and hold on for 2 seconds. Bellkeeper (level 23): the bell tolls three times; after the third, swipe down to lower your head and keep it down until the toll fades. Before each boss level you meet the ghosts you have learned in turn, and the last is the Hollow: it fears the talisman. Glassface (the level 30 boss) fears the hammer, and the Ash Flock fears the bucket. From level 15 on there may be false omens (just a scare), and from level 25 attacks can come back to back.
peek.view.33: Torches, charms and old scrolls appear by the road; tap them when you get close to pick them up. A torch gives 0.6 seconds more warning before the next attack and marks its direction; a charm blocks one fatal mistake. A campfire appears on the 5th level of every ten (every 20% in a free run), where you choose one of three items and rest for a moment. If three levels in a row drop nothing, the next level always drops something. Fog in the graveyard narrows your view, sounds in the swamp are muffled, hiding is slower in the snowfield, and the volcano's picture wavers slightly.
peek.view.34: Fixed rewards: dodge 2 attacks for 2 points; reach the exit and open the box for 5 points. Each is paid once per round, credited on the spot and kept even if you die later; at most 7 points per round. In level mode each level pays only the first time you clear it; replaying cleared levels and practice pay nothing. Score, best progress, the cause-of-death codex and total dodges are for display only and are not exchanged for points. This is an action and reaction game; the result depends on your moves.
peek.view.35: On a phone you can press "Enable motion" to tilt the phone instead of swiping left or right; browsers that do not support it fall back to gestures automatically. The screen contains flashing light; if that bothers you, turn on "Low scare" or do not play. Switching games or background tabs pauses the run and it resumes when you return. Refreshing abandons the run; points already credited are kept. Best progress, causes of death, total dodges, scrolls and options are saved in the browser; points are shared with the other games and have no cash value.
peek.view.36: Don't Peek: auto-run to the exit; swipe left or right to hide beside the road, tap the left or right half when props appear, tap once to pick things up; read the omens and decide how to hide
pet-walk.view.06: BONUS +1 point for every 20 steps, up to 3 points per trip.
pet-walk.view.07: Tap to step, hold to keep walking; Space works too. On a choice event, tap a button; if you do nothing, Space or a short wait picks the default option. While the wheel spins, tap again to stop it, and time it when the pointer lights up for a luck boost.
pet-walk.view.09: Each trip play. Gray walks along the road for 60 steps, split into plains, waters and mountains, 20 steps each. Every few steps a random event appears: Picking up loot, stray dogs, a river shark, falling rocks, or a lucky wheel. After step 60 there is one last wheel at the door. Some events offer a choice, such as headbutting a locker open or prying it with rope, or trading a can for a wheel spin or barking back at the dogs.
pet-walk.view.10: BONUS: Each 20-step segment immediately awards 1 point, once per segment, up to 3 points per walk. All play is and earned rewards are retained after leaving or refreshing. The wheel, supplies and score are gameplay values, not point conversions. This is a reaction and exploration game without wagering.
pet-walk.view.11: After 60 steps Gray writes a diary entry and your collection grows: each new event, rare event or item adds 5 score the first time it appears. Switching games or tabs pauses the game and it resumes when you return. The collection and best score are stored in your browser; points are shared with the other games and have no cash value.
pet-walk.view.12: Pet Walkies: tap to step, hold to keep walking, meet random events and a wheel on the way, and reach home after 60 steps to write a diary
plinko.view.12: Pearls bounce through the pegs and pay the multiplier of their landing bin. You can drop several in succession.
plinko.view.14: At every peg row, a pearl has an equal chance to go left or right. Center bins are therefore more likely; outer bins are rarer. Payout is the bin multiplier × bet. Center multipliers are below 1, while the largest payouts are at the edges.
plinko.view.15: Higher risk means greater losses in the center and higher payouts at the sides. More rows make the outer bins rarer and raise the largest multiplier. Each table uses binomial probabilities and targets an expected return of about 97%; the panel shows the rounded actual value.
plinko.view.16: Browser randomness determines the landing bin when the pearl is dropped; the animation only shows it. Points are shared with the other two games and have no cash value.
pudding.view.07: Gang must carry Pudding to safety! Start, build a weapon and charge ahead.
pudding.view.08: Camp: choose a piece, tap the grid to place it (rotation available), then select Forge. Run: hold
pudding.view.10: ) or hold the screen to move left and right. The weapon grid is your attack range: red blades cut continuously, blue spears thrust, and yellow shields block arrows and reduce Pudding's fright.
pudding.view.12: There are 8 segments. Before each segment, choose one of three pieces (blade, spear or shield) and fit it into a 4×4 weapon grid, overwriting existing cells. Groups of at least 3 connected cells of one color give bonuses. The grid appears in front of Gang and is the actual attack area: Blades deal continuous damage and slow enemies, spears strike and knock them back, and shields block arrows and reduce Pudding's fright.
pudding.view.13: Each segment lasts 16 seconds. Hold arrows or the screen to move Gang into enemies. Collisions, arrows and enemies slipping past reduce Pudding's calm. Every 8 consecutive defeats restore some calm; each segment also restores it on completion. At zero calm Pudding cries and the round ends.
pudding.view.14: Each segment cleared immediately awards 1 point. Clearing all 8 gives 2 extra points (10 total). Credited rewards remain when the round ends. Score does not convert to points. Results depend on weapon layout and movement.
pudding.view.15: Switching games or hiding the tab pauses play; return to continue. Refreshing abandons the round. credited points remain. Your best record is saved in this browser. Points are shared and have no cash value.
pudding.view.16: Pudding Dash: fit a weapon piece before each segment, then hold arrows or the screen to move Gang and strike enemies; escort Prince Pudding to the bridge
quack-pond.view.05: Tap a cell once to mark ✕ (a note), tap again to place a duck. Correct ducks automatically mark impossible cells; a wrong duck costs 1 heart, and the level fails when all 3 are gone. 3 hints per level, no penalty.
quack-pond.view.07: The pond is split into differently colored regions. Every row, every column and every colored region needs exactly 1 duck, and no two ducks may touch, not even diagonally. Each level has exactly one answer, needs no guessing, and can be solved with logic. There are 200 levels, from 5×5 to 9×9, getting bigger and harder as you go.
quack-pond.view.08: More hearts left means more stars (up to 3). Clear a level to unlock the next; progress and stars are saved in this browser.
quack-pond.view.09: This game has no BONUS. Levels and stars are just your record and are not converted to points; there are no bets or multiplier payouts. The first full round (at least 10 seconds) of each game each day earns the platform's fixed completion reward.
quack-pond.view.10: Switching games or tabs pauses the game and it resumes when you come back. Refreshing abandons the level. Points are shared with other games and have no cash value.
reaper.view.10: White souls → Collect in the gold zone
reaper.view.11: Green pass → Stay still and let through
reaper.view.14: The underworld is short-staffed! Collect ordinary souls and let green-pass holders through.

tower.view.14: Climb eight floors from the bottom, choosing one cell per floor. Bubbles advance you and increase the multiplier; an urchin loses the bet. After each safe floor you can collect bet × current multiplier. Reaching the top collects automatically.
tower.view.15: Difficulty determines cells per floor and how many are safe: Easy 4/3, Medium 3/2, Hard 2/1, Extreme 3/1. After eight floors, multipliers are 9.69×, 24.86×, 248.32× and 6,364.17× respectively.
tower.view.16: The multiplier is (cell count ÷ safe cells) raised to the floor number, then multiplied by 0.97, giving an expected return of about 97% regardless of difficulty or collection floor. Urchins are placed using browser randomness when you start. Points are shared with other games and have no cash value.
wheel.view.14: The segment under the top pointer determines the multiplier when the wheel stops.
wheel.view.16: Spin Compass deducts the bet. The segment under the top pointer determines the multiplier: collect bet × multiplier, or lose the bet on 0. All segments are equally likely.
wheel.view.17: Low risk: eight of ten segments pay 1.2× or 1.3× and two pay 0. Medium risk: half pay 0 and half pay 1.5× to 3×. High risk: only one segment pays, at segment count × 0.97 (9.7× for 10, 19.4× for 20, 29.1× for 30). For low and medium risk, segment count changes the divisions, not the odds.
wheel.view.18: All settings have an average segment multiplier of 0.97, giving an expected return of 97%. Browser randomness determines the result when you click; the spin only animates it. Points are shared and have no cash value.

pet-walk.say.051: I met three stray dogs today. We understood each other.

pet-walk.say.058: The mechanic called me an antique today.
pet-walk.say.059: Wrench called me an antique. I haven't forgotten.
pet-walk.say.061: A river shark pops out of the water, jaws wide open!

pet-walk.say.064: The shark spits out not a fish, but an old boot.
pet-walk.say.066: I had a run-in with the river shark today. I remember.
pet-walk.say.067: I haven't forgotten that river shark.
pet-walk.say.069: A mysterious box drifts to shore. Gray drags it up.
pet-walk.say.070: It floated here on its own. I didn't steal it.
pet-walk.say.071: Rhythmic knocking comes from inside the drift box.
pet-walk.say.072: Someone's inside. Let's pretend we didn't hear.
pet-walk.say.073: I found a drift box today. I swear I didn't steal it.
pet-walk.say.074: That drift box last time? Really not stolen.

pet-walk.say.078: Buoy and Gray stare at each other for 3 seconds. Neither blinks.
pet-walk.say.079: I didn't lose. I just didn't win.
pet-walk.say.080: Buoy kept staring at me today.
pet-walk.say.081: Buoy stared at me last time. Not again today.
pet-walk.say.083: Gray is muttering to a rock when the rock suddenly answers.
pet-walk.say.084: This rock is a better talker than me.
pet-walk.say.085: The crab disguises itself as a tiny pebble. Gray finds it anyway.
pet-walk.say.086: It disguised itself as a pebble. I still found it.
pet-walk.say.087: I talked to a rock for a long time today. It's a better talker than me.
pet-walk.say.088: That rock from last time is still a better talker than me.
pet-walk.say.090: A small rock falls from the cliff straight toward Gray's head!
pet-walk.say.091: I'm fine. I meant to do that.
pet-walk.say.092: The fallen pebbles arrange themselves into a smiley face.
pet-walk.say.093: The mountain is laughing at me.
pet-walk.say.094: A rock hit my head today. I meant to do that.
pet-walk.say.095: My head still remembers that rock.

pet-walk.say.098: Gray chases its own antenna in circles.
pet-walk.say.099: Gray falls asleep walking and bumps into a wall.
pet-walk.say.100: Streetlight, I have something to tell you.
pet-walk.say.102: I wasn't sleeping. I was thinking with my eyes closed.
pet-walk.say.103: Gray does all three weird things at once: talks to a streetlight, chases its antenna, sleepwalks.
pet-walk.say.105: I did something strange today. Please don't ask.

pet-walk.say.109: A storm hits and bends Gray's antenna. After the storm, a rainbow appears.
pet-walk.say.110: I'm not scared. Just slightly damp.
pet-walk.say.112: A pigeon is standing on the rainbow.
pet-walk.say.114: It rained today, then a rainbow came. Luck should be on the way.
pet-walk.say.115: There was a rainbow after the rain last time. Maybe again today.

siege-architect.view.04: Drag unit cards onto time slots to set when they depart, then press Attack. Each tower shows its targeting rule; a failed attack keeps your plan so you can tweak it and retry.
siege-architect.view.06: The defenses are set. Now you attack. Schedule when each critter departs on a 10-second timeline, press Attack and watch your plan succeed or fail. Gun towers hit the closest unit, cannons hit the highest HP with a splash, and snipers hit whoever entered range first; a tower keeps firing at its target until it falls or leaves range. There is no randomness: the same plan always gives the same result.
siege-architect.view.07: 20 levels, each with a squad budget and gate HP. Breaching the gate earns 1 star, staying within the cost target earns another, and meeting the level's extra condition earns the third. Clearing a level unlocks the next; progress, stars and plans are saved in this browser.
siege-architect.view.08: This game has no BONUS. Levels and stars are just your record and are not converted to points; there are no bets or multiplier payouts. The first full round (at least 10 seconds) of each game each day earns the platform's fixed completion reward.
siege-architect.view.09: The leaderboard counts the different levels the server has replayed and verified, once per level. Switching games or tabs pauses the attack and it resumes when you return; changing levels or refreshing ends the round but keeps your plan.
